channel.title: Context-Engineering on Harness Engineer
channel.description: Recent content in Context-Engineering on Harness Engineer

item.title: Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
item.description: HumanLayer patterns for reducing context drift and making coding sessions easier to resume.

item.title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
item.description: Manus’ detailed playbook on KV-cache locality, tool masking, filesystem memory, and keeping useful failures in-context.

item.title: Context Engineering for Coding Agents
item.description: Thoughtworks guidance on shaping the task environment so coding agents can stay grounded and productive.

item.title: Context Forking to Save Time, Tokens and Trouble
item.description: Treats the agent context window as a downward-growing OS stack and argues forking/rewind as a core harness primitive for course-correction, parallel design exploration, and salvaging context after context-inefficient operations.

item.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
item.description: Anthropic’s guidance on managing the context window as a working memory budget rather than a dumping ground.

item.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
item.description: Anthropic’s core article on initializer agents, feature lists, init.sh, self-verification, and handoff artifacts across many context windows.

item.title: Harness Engineering
item.description: Thoughtworks’ framing of harness work into context engineering, architectural constraints, and “garbage collection” against entropy.

item.title: Long-Context Isn't the Answer
item.description: Empirical argument that extended-context models degrade instruction adherence at all lengths because the ‘instruction budget’ doesn’t scale with context window size. Makes the case that context isolation (sub-agents, progressive disclosure, backpressure) beats context expansion.

item.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
item.description: Framing a hosted long-horizon agent as a ‘meta-harness’ with stable interfaces (session, harness, sandbox) inspired by OS virtualization. Covers decoupling brain from hands for resumability, many-brains/many-hands scaling, and why the session log — not the context window — is the durable context object.

item.title: Every Agent Needs a Box — Aaron Levie, Box
item.description: Aaron Levie (Box CEO) on the infrastructure every agent needs: sandboxed “box” workspaces, agent identity and governance, permission models for agent-vs-human data access, and why context engineering (not infinite context windows) is the real bottleneck for enterprise knowledge-work agents. Includes Box’s internal agent eval methodology — rubric-scored retrieval across industry document sets — and the explore/exploit search limits of frontier models.
